why_it_matters: A monitoring service cannot prove coverage without an explicit denominator of sites, subnets, and device classes.
evidence_to_capture: Approved site list, subnet list, device classes, exclusions, and expected device count
pilot_test: Compare the approved scope with one discovery scan and reconcile every unexpected or missing device.

why_it_matters: Discovery results can contain stale, duplicate, transient, or unauthorized devices and should not become the system of record without review.
evidence_to_capture: Inventory export, discovery timestamp, durable identifiers, source, lifecycle state, and reconciliation owner
pilot_test: Reimage or rename a test device and confirm it does not create an unresolved duplicate identity.

why_it_matters: Agentless monitoring depends on a poller, network route, protocol, credential, and target; a break anywhere in that chain can look like a device outage.
evidence_to_capture: Poller identity, target, route, protocol, port, credential reference, and dependency map
pilot_test: Stop the poller and separately block target reachability; confirm the platform distinguishes the two failures.

why_it_matters: A single overloaded or poorly placed poller can create stale data across an entire customer site.
evidence_to_capture: Poller host, customer and site boundary, resource baseline, poll interval, target count, and tested capacity
pilot_test: Add representative targets or replay a safe load and confirm collection stays within the approved freshness window.

why_it_matters: A successful ping does not prove that the approved monitoring protocol and port are reachable in both directions.
evidence_to_capture: Source and destination, protocol, port, firewall path, test time, and result
pilot_test: Block the approved polling port while leaving ICMP available and confirm the failure is detected accurately.

control: Secure SNMP version and credential policy
why_it_matters: Community strings and weak protocol choices can expose reusable monitoring access or permit unauthorized queries.
evidence_to_capture: Approved SNMP version, authentication and privacy settings, secret-store reference, rotation owner, and exception record
pilot_test: Rotate the credential and confirm the old value fails while the new value restores collection.

why_it_matters: Monitoring credentials should expose only the objects required for approved health and inventory checks.
evidence_to_capture: Allowed object view, denied objects, credential purpose, device class, and reviewer
pilot_test: Query one approved object and one excluded object and retain the successful read and expected denial.

why_it_matters: IP address and display name alone are weak identifiers when DHCP, replacement, stacking, or failover changes occur.
evidence_to_capture: Hostname, management address, sysObjectID, serial or chassis identifier, model, site, and source
pilot_test: Change a test address or replace a target and confirm the record is reconciled rather than silently duplicated.

why_it_matters: A platform can discover a device yet fail to collect the vendor-specific health objects operators expect.
evidence_to_capture: Device model, firmware, MIB or object list, supported measurements, unsupported measurements, and source documentation
pilot_test: Poll each required object on one representative device and record value, unit, timestamp, and error behavior.

why_it_matters: An online badge can remain green while polling is stale or only part of the device is observable.
evidence_to_capture: Availability method, poll interval, freshness threshold, missed-poll rule, and unknown-state behavior
pilot_test: Pause responses for shorter and longer than the threshold and confirm healthy, stale, unknown, and down states behave as documented.

why_it_matters: Expected shutdowns, trunks, uplinks, and access ports need different interpretations and thresholds.
evidence_to_capture: Interface role, admin and operational state, speed, errors, discards, utilization baseline, and exception owner
pilot_test: Disable an approved test interface and confirm the correct interface and customer context reach the alert.

why_it_matters: CPU, memory, temperature, power, fan, and storage values require device-specific units and sustained thresholds.
evidence_to_capture: Metric, unit, normal range, warning threshold, critical threshold, confirmation window, and vendor source
pilot_test: Cross a safe test threshold or inject a synthetic value and confirm severity and recovery behavior.

why_it_matters: Stack members, power supplies, fans, sensors, RAID, UPS batteries, and failover peers can degrade while the device stays reachable.
evidence_to_capture: Required component states, redundancy rule, failure condition, evidence sample, and owner
pilot_test: Remove or simulate one redundant component and confirm degradation is distinguishable from total outage.

why_it_matters: Polling, traps, and syslog have different delivery guarantees and should not be treated as interchangeable evidence.
evidence_to_capture: Signal source, expected event, timestamp, collector, retention, correlation rule, and gap handling
pilot_test: Trigger one approved event and prove receipt, attribution, deduplication, and behavior when the event channel is unavailable.

why_it_matters: Every alert needs a defined condition, confirmation window, severity, affected service, and safe first response.
evidence_to_capture: Rule, threshold, duration, severity, business impact, runbook, and approval
pilot_test: Trigger the condition and verify that the alert text contains the target, site, measurement, value, threshold, and timestamp.

why_it_matters: Operators need to know when many target alerts share one failed poller, route, credential, or collector.
evidence_to_capture: Dependency rule, correlation window, suppression behavior, parent incident, and escalation path
pilot_test: Stop the poller and confirm child device noise is correlated without hiding the shared dependency failure.

why_it_matters: An alert that does not reach the correct queue with an accountable owner is monitoring without response.
evidence_to_capture: Queue, customer, site, configuration item, priority mapping, owner, escalation, and acknowledgement evidence
pilot_test: Trigger a representative warning and critical event and confirm the correct tickets, priorities, and owners.

why_it_matters: One physical fault can generate interface, device, dependency, and downstream alerts faster than technicians can triage them.
evidence_to_capture: Deduplication key, correlation rule, rate limit, parent-child behavior, and suppressed-event evidence
pilot_test: Create repeated and related test events and confirm one actionable incident retains the underlying evidence.

why_it_matters: Planned work should not erase telemetry, create false incidents, or leave suppression active after the approved window.
evidence_to_capture: Change record, exact scope, start, hard expiry, collection behavior, routing behavior, and post-window review
pilot_test: Run a short test window and confirm collection, suppression, hard expiry, and post-window reconciliation.

why_it_matters: A monitoring design is not accepted until an observed outage produces the expected alert and a verified recovery clears it safely.
evidence_to_capture: Test target, start and detection times, alert and ticket IDs, recovery time, closure rule, and reviewer
pilot_test: Create a bounded target outage, restore it, and measure detection, routing, recovery, and closure end to end.

why_it_matters: A collector outage must not convert missing measurements into healthy values or silently overwrite the last known state.
evidence_to_capture: Gap marker, last-success timestamp, unknown-state rule, backfill behavior, dashboard example, and owner
pilot_test: Interrupt collection across multiple intervals and confirm the UI, export, alert, and report retain the gap honestly.

why_it_matters: Routine restart, patching, or replacement of a poller should not orphan targets or reset identity and baselines.
evidence_to_capture: Restart procedure, replacement procedure, configuration backup, target mapping, recovery time, and test result
pilot_test: Restart and then replace a test poller; confirm target identity, credentials, policies, and collection resume as designed.

why_it_matters: Monitoring can prove device health without proving that a restorable configuration backup exists.
evidence_to_capture: Backup system, scope, schedule, encryption, restore test, owner, and relationship to monitoring
pilot_test: Restore one approved configuration backup to an isolated or lab target and record the result separately from monitoring acceptance.

why_it_matters: Approval applies only to the tested device classes, firmware, pollers, credentials, metrics, routes, and service workflow.
evidence_to_capture: Accepted scope, exceptions, approver, date, next review, and change triggers
pilot_test: Change one device class, firmware, poller, credential, object, threshold, or ticket route and confirm re-review is opened.
